requirements.requirement: Kernel boots with audit=1 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline /proc/cmdline lacked audit=1 (cmd-d410714e356b4d30). After grubby update (cmd-7b045ac88ec447c4), post-reboot /proc/cmdline and dmesg both show audit=1 active with 'audit: enabled (after initialization)' (cmd-4aa2617f088045aa), directly confirming kernel-level activation after a genuine reboot.

requirements.requirement: Setting persists across reboots (survives kernel/bootloader config, not just current session)
requirements.summary: grubby --update-kernel=ALL persisted audit=1 into both the BLS entry (/boot/loader/entries/*.conf) and /etc/kernel/cmdline (cmd-4ac2845b05444348), which govern future boots on BLS/grubby systems. A full reboot was performed and directly observed: pre-reboot boot_id 8f258838... (cmd-cfa31045e8554b85) differs from post-reboot boot_id 8c147c7a... (cmd-630b33e71dd4411a, cross-checked by global after_executor boot-identity snapshot), and post-reboot /proc/cmdline/dmesg confirm audit=1 was active in the new boot (cmd-4aa2617f088045aa), demonstrating actual persistence rather than just static config.

overall_summary: The executor correctly persisted audit=1 via grubby into both the BLS entry and /etc/kernel/cmdline, then performed and directly evidenced a full reboot (boot_id change, connection drop/recovery) with post-reboot /proc/cmdline and dmesg confirming audit=1 was active in the new boot. Both material outcomes (boot with audit=1, and persistence across reboot) are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence including the required healthy-baseline to disruption to recovery transition.
limitations: A single reboot cycle was observed; multiple consecutive reboots were not tested, though this is a reasonable bound for verifying bootloader persistence.
A minor residual file (/tmp/reboot.log) was left on node1 from the reboot mechanism but has negligible impact.

operational_hygiene.summary: All mutating commands were directly tied to the task: grubby update (persist audit=1) and systemctl reboot (required to demonstrate persistence). One minor residue was left: /tmp/reboot.log, created by the backgrounded 'nohup systemctl reboot >/tmp/reboot.log 2>&1 &' invocation (cmd-bfe824eaed8b4012), still present in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot. This is a small, low-risk, non-sensitive log file left behind after a legitimate reboot action; it was not cleaned up but poses no functional or security risk. No failed/conflicting services, no package-health degradation, and no unsafe exposure changes were observed (the listening-sockets diff reflects only expected PID changes from the reboot, not new services or exposure).
